reasoning: Let M be a 4x4 0-1 matrix with all row and column sums 2 and zero diagonal. Consider the complement C = J - M (J = all-ones matrix). C has entries in {0,1}, every row and column sum 4 - 2 = 2, and every diagonal entry equal to 1. Then P = C - I has entries in {0,1} (diagonal entries drop from 1 to 0, off-diagonal unchanged), every row and column sum 1, and zero diagonal. So P is a permutation matrix with no fixed points, i.e. a derangement of {1,2,3,4}. Conversely, given any derangement matrix P, M = J - I - P is a 0-1 matrix with row/column sums 4 - 1 - 1 = 2 and zero diagonal. This is a bijection, so the count equals the number of derangements of 4 elements: D_4 = 4!(1 - 1 + 1/2 - 1/6 + 1/24) = 12 - 4 + 1 = 9. (Cases: 3 derangements that are products of two disjoint transpositions, 6 that are 4-cycles; total 9.) Sanity check: without the diagonal constraint there are 90 such matrices; the diagonal constraint via the complement bijection reduces this to 9.
